subject: How to specify a non-linear interaction with a dummy variable

messages.author: 2051adad79c6db64
messages.subject: How to specify a non-linear interaction with a dummy variable
parts:
dear all
I would like to predict using lincomb the effect of an interaction between a dummy variable and a non-linear function (rw2).
I'm unsure on how to specify correctly my formula and define lincomb.

Basically, I would like to obtain the prediction from a f(., rw2) function by level of a dummy variable


Toy example :
n = 200
a = rep(seq(0, 100, length.out = n / 2), 2)
a2 = a * a
my_dummy = rep(1:2, each = n / 2)
y = my_dummy * (a + 0.1 * a2) + rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 0.5)
data = data.frame(y = y, a = a, my_dummy = my_dummy)

# I'm unsure on the right formula so I tried
formula = y ~ f(a, model = "rw2", replicate = my_dummy) + my_dummy
# and also adding my_dummy as weight
# y ~ f(a, my_dummy, model = "rw2", replicate = my_dummy) + my_dummy

# Trying to generate linear combinations
lc1 = inla.make.lincombs(a = rep(seq(0, 100, length.out = n / 2), 2), my_dummy = rep(1:2, each = n / 2))


result = inla(
  formula,
  data = data,
  family = "gaussian",
  lincomb = lc1,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)
)

I would expect result$summary.lincomb.derived$mean to be close to result$summary.fitted.values and y, which is not the case.
Thanks in advance for any enlightments

ok, if you want to have

beta * x + beta^2 * xx

then you need to code this using 'rgeneric'. see inla.doc("rgeneric")
and the linear regression example, since this is just a model for the
mean.
